body.x: Toonsquare (CEO Lee Ho-young) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri) local time, introducing ‘Tooning Studio’ featuring generative AI technology at the Eureka Park booth.

Toonsquare operates the web browser-based Software as a Service (SaaS) AI artificial intelligence webtoon creation platform called ‘Tooning’ service. Tooning incorporates Toonsquare’s core AI technology optimized for digital creation, including Tooning Editor, Tooning Magic AI (Beta), and Tooning World (Beta) services (as of July 2023).

Tooning Editor is an AI-based content creation service that allows users to create various forms of digital content easily and quickly based on their writing or stories. Additionally, Tooning Magic AI is a high-quality image creation service that allows anyone to generate high-resolution images by clicking on or directly entering prompts needed for image creation within the service.

Tooning World is a platform where users can experience original webtoon content from Tooning and various webtoons and share and post their own created webtoons. In Tooning World, AI is used to develop Webtoons (for all generations) and Toptoons (for adults), offering Webtoons created with AI and Webtoons by professional artists and allowing readers to share their works.

By integrating Toonsquare’s natural language processing AI technology (NLP: Natural Language Processing), which includes ‘emotion analysis’ and ‘morpheme analysis,’ with image-generating AI models such as Stable Diffusion and ChatGPT, Toonsquare explains that it can reduce working hours in the digital content production process and enhance the completeness of digital content. Furthermore, Tooning is creating a low-cost, high-quality webtoon production environment by applying Toonsquare’s Webtoon auto-generation AI technology to the existing webtoon production process.

body.cap: Toonsquare booth at CES 2024 Eureka Park │Photo by AVING News

body.x: In the future, Toonsquare plans to release the web browser-based ‘Tooning Magic AI’ (SaaS) beta globally, not only in Korea but also centered around the United States.

Regarding this, Lee Ho-young, CEO of Toonsquare, who met with Aving News at CES 2024, said, “Visitors to our booth are already familiar with and have experience using generative AI, making the meetings at the exhibition meaningful. Many visitors asked specific questions based on their experience with various generative AIs.” He also expressed hope to meet companies with expertise in collaboration or research through this exhibition and ongoing research projects with an AI company in Canada that learns emotions.

He added, “This participation goes beyond a simple exhibition; it has become a space for exchanging generative AI technology. Through networking among leaders, experts, and practitioners in the generative AI field, Toonsquare had in-depth discussions on the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem. Such exchanges will play an important role not only in the technological development of Toonsquare but also in promoting innovation throughout the AI industry.” He further emphasized that direct feedback from users received during this exhibition would be a valuable asset in advancing AI technology and products.

Regarding plans, CEO Lee mentioned, “Especially at CES, there was strong interest from investors, leading to more secondary meetings upon returning to Korea. This is evidence that Toonsquare’s growth potential has been recognized internationally, and we can now anticipate expectations for future development.” He concluded that all these experiences catalyze solidifying Toonsquare’s capabilities in ‘generative AI technology,’ ‘hustle and passion as a startup,’ and beyond, fostering ‘ambitious dreams.’ Based on this foundation, Toonsquare will continue to pursue innovation and explore the path of new possibilities.

body.x: CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
